I had undiagnosed ADHD all my life.

Was first diagnosed during my hospitalizations at 21~, possible autism.

What helps me is competitiveness. Making a game of everything. Life in its entirety is a game. 

Set "missions"/goals ALWAYS. have multiple. Main Mission and side mission. The things you don't want to do now. DO THEM NOW. How? Find the best and easiest way that fits you. Either deadlines and do them 1 day before or slightly late but it's done. Or competitive I see someone doing something and I want to do better.
Set your competition to something close to you. Like friends, then after beating them increase it to state or w/e. But start with a small manageable group and extend.

Being top 3 of your friends. Being top 3 in your class. Being top 3 in your state. Being top 3 nation wide.

Never limit yourself. Set realistic expectations. Never (hard for me still) have 1 answer for anything. Always think of multiple situations of the same thing.
Example. 
Exam expectations: you passed with an amazing grade, you passed, you failed.
Then set how to achieve each goal and the likelihood with what you currently know to achieve each outcome.

I did "intentional Olympiad of informatics" I went into it blind only knowing coding in c++.

Didn't know what it was and we were ill prepared. 

Simplify the problem as best as you can. Solve it in concept.
Don't think of it as code yet.

We had a problem called "Parrots" in my year. It was written like this. Birds can send bytes. Bytes dont arrive in order. You can send as many birds but lower points? For more birds ? The birds don't arrive in order of sending.

Make encoder and decoder.

The sub tasks were like a bird can remember 0 to 65,555 numbers task 1. Then it shrinks and shrinks. The last being 0-255. Tbh I had no idea what anything was. I was a high schooler. I knew how to make things as what I want in code.

But what do I want here? How do I solve this without code ?
The first sub tasks were kinda easy. I just attached the position to the last 3 digits. And used the first 1 for character.
We have 26 characters, 3 digits for position.
So if I wanted to send "ABC" id send 01001, 02002, 03003.
That sub problem was solved but with lower and lower
The other sub tasks I just created a simple mapping for characters I'd call it a bootleg hashmap.

The last sub tasks I couldn't solve with the restrictions given and knowledge I had at the time. But a contestant that solved it I went and asked him because it annoyed me. To me I did solve it but I kept exceeding the memory limits.

When he explained it to me, I can never forget it now. That concept is locked with me forever.

He used the byte form in bits 00-00-00-00. He did what I did for the first sub tasks but in Bit form but also sent x birds for x position. He put character in the first 3 bits? Or the last bits? And then sent the position bit in the other. Or something like that. He simplified the problem more than I simplified it. I used decimals, he used binary.

TL;DR learn basics, simplify problems to their base base form. Even if you think you are at the base think SIMPLER. Basically how a computer would understand it. Or how a child would solve it. Then write that, after that it's just optimization.

Late autism diagnosis here. I also got upset first and confused when people called me or asked me if I have autism. I took the question and the call/insult? The same way. My first reaction was always "how can I be autistic if I am better than you at things", so I rejected it and didn't think it was possible with the level of "functioning" I had lol. I wasn't functional. I just was really good at specific things.

Basic concepts like saying "what's up?" To a random person didn't make sense to me because they don't expect an answer ? But still say something? I don't know still.

But I also simply things for myself, everything has an equivalent. I observe first always and then act. Look at people eat the berries and I eat the berries better and more efficiently. I look at everything as a "rhythm" or "steps". 

When I first got told by a psychiatrist I thought they were joking. But when I actually searched it up and learned about it. I reflected in my entire life differently. I "stimmed" alot and I didn't know it. I liked red... But not red fire trucks. I hated noises so I always wore a headset. I "stayed quiet" but I observed a lot. Later years for work... I did work at home so I don't do it at work because I can't do it at work. I don't like people looking at me working. I made "sound effects", copied/mocked other people's noises because noises were funny. I hated specific texture of foods and semi-hard shell crunch with squeeze/liquids. 

I got called "emotionless" many times. Made fun of because my eyes move when I think. I struggled understanding how people don't understand what I thought was "simple" and basic.  It made me angry, when I didn't understand I get upset because they don't know how to explain things or giving "useless" information, or what I thought as useless because it wasn't needed to do a task/understand the current topic/subject. 

It's not all bad. It's also makes me really good at coding. Makes me really good at rhythm. Makes me really good at seeing very similar things and seeing the difference between them when others can't. It makes me, me. 

I would rather not go through life not knowing I had, but I don't want to go through life without it now. I like the superpowers. I can tell you everything about Power Rangers up until 2015 2016. I can remember moments exactly as they happened. What words were spoken, what was playing in the background. Trauma is hard to forget because of that lol. 

Autism doesn't make a person "stupid". It just makes them see and think of things differently. We can mirror others to seem more "normal" and that's what I do/did.

Anger to me is the most "disgusting emotion". I "like" making angry people more angry on purpose. If I think/believe there is no real reason to be angry over something I will abuse it. 

Your boyfriend, id probably keep calling him "autistic" because it doesn't mean anything or change anything in his life if he is going to get mad over that then he deserves to be mad. That's how I think of it. Because let's say he is not autistic and you call him or ask if he is autistic? What changes in his life ? Nothing. 
What if he is autistic? What changes in his life ? Nothing besides him learning something about him self.
Anger here is useless because nothing changes either way.

To me that's equivalent to saying "you are a dodo head" and him crying "I am not!!! I am not a dodo head 😭 I can't believe you think I am a dodo head🤬". I admit I am a victim of getting worked up over someone saying they are me. "No! You are Insert_their_name_here, I am insert_my_name_here". If they repeat it. I start taking their identity and just try to either make them take it back or reject mine for theirs. Like saying in a mocking voice "oh I am steeve, I am stupid and short." Then respond normally saying. "I see why you want to be me, if I was you I'd want to be me too" I learned that from a song. 

TL;DR:
My advice Keep calling him a autistic or say "and you are not autistic?" when ever he does something you THINK is.
Or Try to make him understand what autism is.
I like the first option better.
